member.name: T:OpenIGI.Audio.OpenAL.OpenAlAudioDevice
member.summary: An on OpenAL Soft, through Silk.NET.

remarks.para: The original drives DirectSound directly and hand-computes every sound's apparent position into volume, pan and playback frequency (0x496E60). This backend can do either: with off it feeds OpenAL the gain and pan produces, and with it on it hands over the position and lets OpenAL place the sound properly.

The distance model is linear in both profiles. OpenAL's computes exactly the fade the original does — full gain inside the reference distance, a straight line to silence at the maximum, clamped either side — so the min and max distances the game's own data carries keep meaning what their authors intended. Choosing an inverse model instead would be more physical and less faithful, and would quietly retune every sound in the game.

Divergence, and it is audible if you go looking: OpenAL has no per-channel gain for a mono source, so the vanilla profile's pan is approximated by placing the source on a unit circle around the listener rather than by attenuating one output channel by an exact number of millibels. The gain curve is exact — it goes through the original's own table — but the stereo image is a close likeness rather than a reproduction. Making it exact would mean owning the mixer.
The voice pool, stealing, handles and stream refills are 's, shared with every other backend; what is here is only what OpenAL itself needs to be told.
If no device can be opened the object still constructs and behaves as silence, with false. Nothing about a missing sound card may stop the game booting.

member.content: The time warp: every voice slowed and muffled at once, through OpenAL's pitch and, where the driver has the effects extension (ALC_EXT_EFX), a low-pass filter on each source's direct path.
member.remarks: The extension's entry points are looked up by name rather than through a binding of their own: three calls and a handful of constants, from the OpenAL 1.1 effects extension's specification. A driver without it still slows; it only does not muffle.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Audio.OpenAL.OpenAlAudioDevice.SetDistances(Silk.NET.OpenAL.AL,System.UInt32,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary: Sets a source's distance range, keeping the two distances apart.
member.remarks: The two must never be equal. The distance model in force is , whose gain is 1 - rolloff * (d - reference) / (max - reference). An equal pair makes that a division by zero: the result is a NaN gain, and a NaN gain is silence, not loudness. A flat voice wants no attenuation at all and the obvious way to ask for it -- reference and max both one, rolloff zero -- is exactly the case that breaks, because the zero rolloff multiplies a NaN rather than replacing it. Separating the two and leaving the rolloff at zero asks for the same thing safely.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Audio.OpenAL.OpenAlVoice
member.summary: One slot in the device's voice pool: a that owns an OpenAL source.
member.remarks: A slot owns its source for the whole life of the device — sources are created once at startup and reused, because creating one per sound would make a firefight allocate hundreds a second. The allocation, stealing and handle bookkeeping is the pool's; only the OpenAL names live here.
